address: WG-plein 600 (former Wilhelmina Gasthuis pavilion), Amsterdam-West: 1931 dark-brown brick hospital wing, five storeys of grouped white windows on the WG-plein side and a two-storey canal front with glazed bay windows on the Kostverlorenvaart
notes: WG-plein 600 (BAG, built 1931) is a pavilion of the former Wilhelmina Gasthuis: a dark-brown brick wing of five storeys on the WG-plein side and two storeys over a basement on the Kostverlorenvaart, with later glazed rooftop boxes and bay windows. 539 wall surfaces. The LoD2.2 shell has 12.8 m of open edge (seven short step walls between the roof levels); shellRepair closes all of it with 7 strips.

walls[0] = panels 10, 189 and 60 (w02-157): the five-storey WG-plein fronts. 5 storeys x 9 bays of white cross windows (the photographed groups of three), with a cornice. The low end surfaces 60 and 447 (18.7 m tops) stay blank so that the eaves gate reads the main roof.

walls[1] = panel 18 (w01-337): the 89 m canal front. Two storeys of cross windows (18 bays) over a blank basement, with a cornice. Simplified: the projecting glazed bay windows and the rooftop glass boxes are the 3DBAG masses in the wall brick.
